Renee Good was a U.S. citizen who was shot and killed in Minneapolis by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer or agent. The descriptions consistently indicate that the death occurred in early 2026 and that ICE was directly involved in the shooting. Some accounts specify that the killing was carried out by an ICE officer, while others refer more generally to ICE agents, but they all describe the same incident in Minneapolis.

Renee Good’s death was reported as having preceded subsequent protests, suggesting that the killing became a notable public event. The available descriptions do not provide additional personal details beyond identifying Renee Good as a U.S. citizen and the victim of a fatal shooting by ICE in Minneapolis.

[PERSON] Bovino
Bovino is a former Border Patrol commander at large who appears in footage from Minneapolis and Chicago, where he was seen with Hewson and identified as being near EZ-17. He is also described as accompanying EZ-17 and EZ-2 on raids in Minnesota and as being alongside EZ-17 at an incident in Illinois. These descriptions place him in multiple force-related incidents in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Illinois.

Bovino is further described as having instigated confrontations and later stating in an Illinois deposition that he did not believe those actions constituted a use-of-force incident. In connection with one event, he was said to have thrown a tear gas canister after being hit on the head and struck by objects thrown by protesters. He was also ordered by Judge Ellis to turn over use-of-force reports and body camera footage.

[PERSON] EZ-17
EZ-17 is a Border Patrol officer and masked federal agent based out of El Paso, identifiable by the uniform number patch EZ-17 and described as wearing a BORTAC vest. He is characterized as an elite Border Patrol officer and was identified by multiple sources, including Unraveled, Bellingcat, and Evident Media, with identification supported through vehicle-interior footage and a Facebook image comparison. One description also names him as Edgar Vazquez.

EZ-17 was involved in several law-enforcement actions captured on video. He was seen firing less lethal munitions, including multiple shots and launcher use, passing a tear gas canister to Bovino, and moving alongside other agents. He was also described as physically pushing protesters, reloading, and standing inside the crime scene tape perimeter near Bovino.
